BiblicalUsage: The word betsa means plunder, unjust gain, and it appears 23 times across the Bible. Judah asked what profit there was in killing Joseph, Samuel's sons turned aside after lucre, and the kings of Canaan took no gain of money.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe greedy gain always costs more than it brings, and that honest work is the only gain that lasts. That is why I keep coming back to it: betsa is not a word to rush past.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
